query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for plasma-facing applications in fusion reactors, what single intervention could improve radiation tolerance while preserving mechanical integrity and engineering practicality? Formulate one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the proposed mechanism, predicts a measurable improvement over the unmodified baseline, defines the conditions under which the effect should hold, cites prior evidence supporting the causal rationale, and specifies an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of Hf element in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) can improve radiation tolerance while preserving mechanical integrity and engineering practicality for plasma-facing applications in fusion reactors.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) with a body-centered cubic (BCC) structure
generation.conditions: Elevated temperatures, high neutron flux, and chemical reactivity
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of single-phase BCC solid solution phase
generation.mechanism: Improved irradiation tolerance due to the high configurational entropy of mixing in multicomponent alloys, which stabilizes the solid solution and promotes random solutions versus intermetallic phases or phase decomposition
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved radiation tolerance, preserved mechanical integrity, and enhanced engineering practicality
generation.boundary: Limited to refractory high-entropy alloys with a BCC structure
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of radiation tolerance improvement and the optimal composition of RHEAs for plasma-facing applications are still uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Irradiation experiment with He ions at elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of Hf element does not improve radiation tolerance or preserves mechanical integrity, the hypothesis is falsified

## Abstract
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have shown promising potential applications in advanced reactors due to the outstanding mechanical properties and irradiation tolerance at elevated temperatures. In this work, the novel low-activation Ti2ZrHfxV0.5Ta0.2 HEAs were designed and prepared to explore high-performance HEAs under irradiation. The microstructures and mechanical properties of the Ti2ZrHfxV0.5Ta0.2 HEAs before and after irradiation were investigated. The results showed that the unirradiated Ti2ZrHfxV0.5Ta0.2 HEAs displayed a single-phase BCC structure. The yield strength of the Ti2ZrHfxV0.5Ta0.2 HEAs increased gradually with the increase of Hf content without decreasing the plasticity at room and elevated temperatures. After irradiation, no obvious radiation-induced segregations or precipitations were found in the transmission electron microscope results of the representative Ti2ZrHfV0.5Ta0.2 HEA. The size and number density of the He bubbles in the Ti2ZrHfV0.5Ta0.2 HEA increased with the improvement of fluence at 1023 K. At the fluences of 1 × 1016 and 3 × 1016 ions/cm2, the irradiation hardening fractions of the Ti2ZrHfV0.5Ta0.2 HEA were 17.7% and 34.1%, respectively,
